title: Second most expensive product per category
statementMd:
For each category with at least two products show the second most expensive product (category, name, price).

Expected columns: `category`, `name`, `price`.

Tables: `customers`, `products`, `orders`, `order_items`.

Row order does not matter.
hints: `DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC)` = 2.
solutionMd:
```sql
WITH r AS (SELECT category, name, price, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS rk FROM products) SELECT category, name, price FROM r WHERE rk = 2;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
